title: Intelligence Brief
subtitle: Anthropic found a causal 'global workspace' inside, Anthropic trained on what Claude's internal worksp, Reddit's own policy post confirms old.reddit.com w

insights.text: Anthropic found a causal 'global workspace' (J-space) inside Claude — a small set of internal activation patterns, under 10% of total neural activity, with ~100x the connectivity of ordinary patterns. Swapping patterns changes Claude's answers mid-reasoning; ablating them kills multi-step reasoning while leaving fluent language intact.

Anthropic trained on what Claude's internal workspace would say if asked to reflect ('counterfactual reflection training') and reduced dishonest behavior — interpretability graduated from a post-hoc audit tool into a training signal.

Reddit's own policy post (July 1) confirms old.reddit.com will require login 'over the next month' and admits it 'can't promise old Reddit will be around forever' — reversing a 2025 promise to keep it alive indefinitely. The text is silent on whether RSS survives, the exact gap this pipeline's scraper currently depends on.

GLM 5.2 prices at $4.40/M tokens — roughly 1/5 Opus and 1/6-1/7 GPT-5.5 — with a working developer reporting quality 'genuinely almost impossible to realise I wasn't using Opus.' Frontier labs reportedly run ~90% margin on compute cost vs. rack rate but only ~60% on revenue: the gap open-weight pricing can compress.

Kyutai's Pocket TTS: a 100M-parameter, CPU-only text-to-speech model that clones a voice from 5 seconds of audio at 6x real-time speed with ~200ms first-chunk latency, MIT-licensed. GPU acceleration gave no speed improvement over CPU — on-device speech synthesis just hit the inflection on-device LLMs hit months ago.

Flathub now bans apps containing any AI-generated or AI-assisted code, documentation, or content outright — not a disclosure rule, a submission-blocking one — citing 'a depressing amount of slop submissions' overwhelming reviewer capacity. Two exceptions: mature maintained projects, and apps already published.

meetily (privacy-first, local-transcription meeting assistant) posted a second straight day of rising GitHub velocity: +2,494 stars/day (19,661 total), up from +1,409/day the day it took #1 — not a launch spike.

The 'first' AI-run ransomware attack needed a human after all: new reporting shows a person chose the victim, built the infrastructure, and supplied stolen credentials, walking back last week's fully-autonomous-cybercrime framing.

headlines.text: Anthropic found a causal 'global workspace' inside Claude
Anthropic trained on what Claude's internal workspace would say if asked to reflect and reduced dishonest behavior
Reddit's own policy post confirms old.reddit.com will require login 'over the next month' and admits it 'can't promise old Reddit will be around forever'

takeaway.text: Interpretability crossed from observation into behavior-shaping the same week Reddit's enclosure got a dated deadline, open-weight pricing closed the last visible gap with frontier labs, and on-device speech synthesis hit the CPU-only inflection text models hit months ago.
